content.comment_body: Hello everyone, My client owns a [product_name] with display, featuring 8 digital inputs and 4 digital outputs. There was no program installed, so I recreated the logic from the machine sequence since I didn’t have the source code. I used [product_name] software in ladder diagram mode for simulation and, due to a lack of interface cable, manually entered the program using the control panel keypad. The program worked as expected. I've attached my program. The issue arises after powering off for one day; upon restart, one line in the program at Q1 is changed (I1-----[ Q1). After checking the system and cycling the power for 10 minutes, everything is fine, but after a day of being off, the same issue repeats at Q1. Can someone explain why only one program line disappears? I’m confused. Thank you!

Hi, This behavior isn’t typical for a [product_name]. The program itself shouldn’t be the cause, but you can test further with a simple program to be sure. It seems like a memory issue, as programs are stored in EEPROM. What is the exact type of your device ([article_no]) and its age? Do any other outputs display similar issues? Regards,
The product code is [article_no] and it’s about 5 years old. I’m still dealing with this problem. Any advice?

Hi, This further suggests a memory problem. See [url] for information on whether the program can be lost after power failure. The best solution may be to replace the [product_name], as repair costs can be higher. Regards,
Thank you for your assistance! I decided to train operators to re-enter the program whenever it fails, rather than replacing the unit.
Hi, That’s an approach I hadn’t considered. Let’s hope the device doesn’t have more issues in the future. Regards,

I’ve experienced that twice on different devices—complete loss of the program after power-off. Instead of always retraining someone to rewrite the program, a better solution may be to use an old memory card for your [product_name]. You can transfer the program to the memory card and insert it into the device; each time it powers up, it loads the program from the memory card to internal memory. The challenge is finding a compatible memory card, as I'm uncertain whether newer models work with the older [article_no] version.
Consider using an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) or replacing the device entirely.

analysis.insight_summary: Multiple users report program loss or corruption on the [product_name] with display ([article_no]), usually after long power outages. Although the programmed logic works well for short power interruptions, extended disconnections lead to partial loss or changes in the program, indicating possible aging or limitations of internal memory hardware. Community members propose hardware replacement, using external memory cards, or backup power solutions to prevent recurrence.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] to consistently retain programming even after long-term power loss. Persistent, reliable memory storage and secure, predictable behavior are desired to ensure the logic remains intact and the device functions as programmed.
